clause_evidence.reasoning: Every one of the twenty samples explicitly asks learners to represent a specific fraction by shading parts of a visual model. The core action of representing—naming, identifying, and depicting—runs throughout all samples without exception or incompleteness.

All twenty samples center on fractional representation, explicitly naming numerators and denominators in stems, answers, and hint text. Each sample presents a fraction in the form of a numerator over a denominator, demonstrating the full scope of fractional notation required at this grade level.

Five samples explicitly represent fractions equal to one: 8/8 (seed 43), 5/5 (seed 45), 6/6 (seed 601), 3/3 (seed 700), and 4/4 (seed 901). In each, the numerator equals the denominator, and the shading of all parts of each unit shape demonstrates that one whole is represented, fulfilling this competency requirement without gaps.

Fifteen samples represent fractions greater than one: 5/3 (seed 42), 9/5 (seed 44), 8/3 (seed 46), 14/6 (seed 500), 18/8 (seed 501), 8/4 (seed 502), 11/6 (seed 600), 3/2 (seed 602), 11/3 (seed 701), 19/6 (seed 702), 17/10 (seed 800), 16/10 (seed 900), 19/6 (seed 1000), 7/3 (seed 1001), and 6/5 (seed 1002). In all cases, the numerator exceeds the denominator, and visual models using multiple divided shapes demonstrate this concept, fully satisfying the competency requirement.

All twenty samples use the FractionShade visual model, which provides identical divided shapes for learners to shade in order to represent the target fraction. This model-based approach is consistent across every sample, enabling learners to develop visual intuition for fractional quantity and fulfilling the competency requirement to use models.
